subject: QuickCart throughput spike — sync, customer comms, and priority decisions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: SRE Team <sre@redwood.ai>, Eng Core <eng-core@redwood.ai>, Customer Success <cs@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuickCart throughput spike — need rapid sync and customer note

Team —

Quick summary: QuickCart reported a ~4x drop in throughput for their Gen API between 08:40–08:55 PDT, with P95 latency increasing from ~180ms to >1.2s. They see elevated tail latency and dropped requests. They are current Dedicated customers on the reserved-GPU pool (pool-id: redwood-dedicated-eus-10).

Immediate asks:
- Ben / SRE: can you confirm if this is a serving runtime issue, autoscaler misbehavior, or a routing problem?
- Karthik / Eng: if kernel scheduling or KV-cache eviction is suspected, we need a short mitigation plan (config change, throttling, or temporary scale-up).
- CS / Olga: prepare a 30-min customer note acknowledging we're investigating and expected follow-up within 60 minutes.
- Jonas / Ops: if we need cross-region fallback, advise on warm capacity and rollout risk.

I attached the initial heap snapshot and an ops timeline where I pasted QuickCart's observation logs. I'll start drafting a customer-facing note after the first triage.

Marissa
Product Lead, Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachments: heap_snapshot_0512.json (7.2MB), ops_timeline_0512.csv (45KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, SRE Team <sre@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuickCart throughput spike — need rapid sync and customer note

Quick triage update —

What we see so far:
- Between 08:38–08:56 PDT a small subset of requests started queueing in front of the gen-worker pool. The scheduler shows batch sizes spiking and several worker containers hitting a GC pause pattern.
- Autoscaler attempted to add pods at 08:44, but they failed readiness checks because a new kernel module (recent runtime tweak) increases cold-start CPU and caused container initialization to cross the readiness timeout.

Initial mitigation performed at 09:18:
- Increased readiness timeout for the affected deployment by 30s (temporary).
- Forced a rolling restart of 6/24 pods to re-establish healthy leaders.

Next steps (15/30/60):
- 15m: continue restarts, monitor P50/P95.
- 30m: if we see >20% of pods failing readiness or P95 > 800ms, roll back the kernel tweak to previous release (rollback plan is ready).
- 60m: if no stabilization, prepare cross-region routing to the warm fallback in us-west-2.

I attached a heap snapshot for the restarted pod and a short ops timeline.

Ben Carter
SRE Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: heap_snapshot_0512.json

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuickCart throughput spike — need rapid sync and customer note

Thanks Ben — following up from Eng perspective.

Root cause hypothesis: the recent runtime kernel selector change (deploy 2027-05-10) introduced a code path that increases JIT compilation work under certain sequence-length distributions. For QuickCart's typical workload (many short prompts with occasional long context), this causes CPU bursts and longer cold start initializations.

Planned engineering actions:
- Immediate (now): revert the kernel selector change on the affected variant (we have a tested rollback image, tagging: runtime-v2.3.1-prev). This should remove the extra CPU pressure. Target: complete revert within 45 minutes.
- Short term (24–48h): add a runtime guard to detect sequence-length distribution and avoid the heavy JIT path for small-batch high-qps customers.
- Roadmap ask: add a canary that simulates QuickCart's traffic pattern during future kernel selector releases.

Impact/risk: Revert is low-risk (no data migration). We will coordinate with SRE for a staged rollback and monitor without autoscaler changes initially. If pods still fail readiness due to heavy initialization, widen readiness timeout as Ben suggested.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi team / Daniel —

Thanks for the quick updates. Below is a short customer-facing note I drafted; please flag edits. I kept it high level and transparent about actions without promising timeline-specific SLAs beyond our immediate checks.

-- draft start --
Hi Daniel / QuickCart team,

We’re investigating a transient throughput degradation affecting some Gen API requests this morning. Our engineers have identified a runtime change that likely increased cold-start CPU demand for your workload pattern. We have taken immediate mitigation steps (restarts and increased readiness timeout) and are preparing a rollback of the recent runtime selector change to remove the extra initialization work.

What to expect next:
• We will provide an update within 60 minutes with stabilization status.
• If needed, we will route traffic to a warm fallback region to maintain throughput.
• No customer data was exposed or changed.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience — we will follow up with a full incident summary once stabilized.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
-- draft end --

Notes: please confirm we can say "rollback of runtime selector change" publicly; if legal/PM prefer different phrasing, advise. Also attaching a suggested one-paragraph internal summary for leadership.

Olga

Olga — thanks, that draft looks good. Two clarifications before sending externally:
1) Replace the phrase "rollback of the runtime selector change" with "reverting a recent runtime optimization" per legal/PM preferences.
2) Add a line: "We will share a post-incident summary with root cause and mitigations within 24 hours."

Decision log (internal):
- Immediate: proceed with Karthik's revert plan (runtime-v2.3.1-prev).
- Mitigation: keep readiness timeout widened and continue rolling restarts.
- Escalation trigger: if P95 remains >800ms after revert + 30m, execute cross-region routing to warm fallback (us-west-2).

Olga, please send the edited note to QuickCart (Daniel) and paste the outbound note here. Ben / Karthik / Jonas: keep monitoring and post short updates to this thread.

Marissa
